source.author: stat
source.text: Herculeis pressum sic fama lacertis terrigenam sudasse Libyn, cum fraude reperta raptus in excelsum, nee iam spes ulla cadendi, nec licet extrema matrem contingere planta, fit sonus, et laetos attollunt agmina plausus, tunc alte librans inopinum sponte remisit obliquumque dedit, procumbentemque secutus colla simul dextra, pedibus simul inguina vinxit.
source.text_original: Herculeis pressum sic fama lacertis / terrigenam sudasse Libyn, cum fraude reperta / raptus in excelsum, nee iam spes ulla cadendi, / nec licet extrema matrem contingere planta, / fit sonus, et laetos attollunt agmina plausus, / tunc alte librans inopinum sponte remisit / obliquumque dedit, procumbentemque secutus / colla simul dextra, pedibus simul inguina vinxit.
source.text_english: So the story goes that the earthborn Libys, crushed by Hercules’ arms, sweated thus: when the trick was discovered, he was snatched up high, and now there was no hope of falling, nor was it possible to touch his mother earth with the last step. Then there was a sound, and the ranks raised joyful applause. Then, balancing him high, he of his own accord let him go unexpectedly and gave him a sideways swing, and following as he fell, he at once bound his neck with his right hand and his groin with his feet.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: at tibi collectas solvit iam fibula vestes ostenditque umeros fortes spatiumque superbi pectoris Herculeis aequum, Meleagre, lacertis.
reuse.text_original: at tibi collectas solvit iam fibula vestes / ostenditque umeros fortes spatiumque superbi / pectoris Herculeis aequum, Meleagre, lacertis.
reuse.text_english: But for you the buckle now loosens the gathered garments and reveals your strong shoulders and the expanse of your proud chest, equal to Hercules’ arms, Meleager.
